newsitem.title: EGYPT: General Silos shares fixed at 39.00 pounds.
newsitem.headline: General Silos shares fixed at 39.00 pounds.

text.p: The initial offer price for privatised shares in General Silos and Storage was fixed at 39.00 pounds a share in a "price discovery" operation at the Egyptian stock exchange on Tuesday, brokers said.
The state had offered four million shares -- 40 percent of the company -- at a minimum price of 37.00 pounds a share.
Two million were on offer to individuals, one million to institutions and mutual funds and one million to the Employee Shareholder Association, which buys on behalf of workers.

The brokers said they did not yet know how many shares the state eventually sold but they doubted it would be more than the 40 percent because the company, which stores and transports wheat for subsidised bread, is in the "strategic" category.

Under the "price discovery" method, the exchange allocates shares to the highest bidders first and then works down the list of bidders until it runs out of shares. Everyone pays the price bid for the last batch of shares.
Most previous Egyptian privatisations have been at a fixed price set by the state.
Brokers said the method and the fact that the state intends to retain majority control of the company dampened demand.
